title: Death Report
summary: Gerald Ashcombe collapsed at the tea table at 16:40 and died.
details: Gerald Ashcombe, 61, complained of his heart racing at 16:38 and collapsed at 16:40. Pronounced dead by Dr Warren at 17:05. The drawing room was sealed.

title: Toxicology Report
summary: A massive dose of pharmaceutical digoxin, from ground tablets. Not foxglove.
details: Digoxin, pharmaceutical grade, from crushed 0.25mg tablets, taken within the hour before death. No plant glycosides present: this did not come from foxgloves.

title: Gerald's Teacup
summary: A gritty residue of crushed tablets in Gerald's cup, and no one else's.
details: Residue of crushed digoxin tablets in the dregs of the deceased's cup. The other three cups and the teapot are clean. The poison went into one cup, not the pot.

title: Mrs Hobbs's Statement
summary: The housekeeper saw Fairlie pour Gerald's cup himself at 16:18, and Lady Constance in the pantry at 15:50.
details: 'When I came back with the hot water at eighteen minutes past, Mr Fairlie was at the sideboard pouring Mr Gerald's cup himself and taking it over to him. He's never poured a cup of tea in this house in thirty years. And her ladyship was in my pantry at ten to four.'

title: Wine Merchant's Delivery Docket
summary: At 16:05 the gardener left the garden to move a car off the drive for the van.
details: Harlow's Wine Merchants: 'Delivered 16:05, Ashcombe Hall. Gardener moved a visitor's black car off the drive to let the van through.'

title: Silas Brook's Account
summary: At 16:10 Fairlie left the reading and went to his car, and was in the glovebox.
details: 'When I went to shift the black Humber, Mr Fairlie came out of the house like a man in a hurry, ten past four, and got into the passenger side with his head in the glovebox. Jumped like a cat when he saw me. Said he'd come for his spectacles. He was wearing them.'

title: The Colonel's Digoxin, in Fairlie's Glovebox
summary: The Colonel's own bottle of digoxin, hidden in Fairlie's car. Eighteen tablets missing.
details: A chemist's bottle labelled for Col. E. Ashcombe: digoxin 0.25mg, 60. Forty-two remain. Eighteen tablets, crushed, is far more than a lethal dose. Fresh prints on the bottle match Ambrose Fairlie.

title: Medicine Handover Receipt
summary: On 10 July the nurse handed all the Colonel's medicines, including 60 digoxin, to Fairlie.
details: '10 July. All remaining medicines of the late Col. Ashcombe handed to Mr A. Fairlie for the probate inventory, incl. digoxin 0.25mg x 60.' Signed: A. Mora; received, A. Fairlie.

title: Saccharin Tin and Diet Card
summary: Lady Constance is diabetic. Her saccharin is kept in the pantry.
details: A chemist's tin of saccharin and a doctor's diet card in Lady Constance's name. She fetches it herself; she won't let the staff touch it.

title: Cut Foxgloves
summary: A dozen foxgloves cut from the border on the morning of the reading.
details: Twelve stems cut cleanly for the drawing-room vases on Saturday morning. Every part of a foxglove is poisonous.

title: Bank Letter to the Trustee
summary: The Ashcombe trust account is overdrawn by £41,212. The bank wrote to Fairlie on 2 July.
details: Ridgeway Savings Bank to A. Fairlie, trustee: 'The Ashcombe family trust account stands overdrawn by £41,212 ... we must ask for your proposals within the month.' Dated 2 July.

title: The Colonel's Will
summary: Gerald executor of the trust, directed to examine its accounts 'forthwith'.
details: 'I leave Ashcombe Hall and the residue of my estate to my brother Gerald, whom I appoint executor and trustee of the family trust, and I direct him to examine the trust accounts forthwith, and to take such advice as he sees fit.' A small annuity to his widow.

title: Probate Inventory
summary: Fairlie's own inventory records receiving the 60 digoxin tablets from the nurse.
details: In Fairlie's hand: 'Medicines received from nurse (A. Mora) 10 July: digoxin 0.25mg, 60 tablets. To be destroyed.' No record of destruction.

title: The Housemaid's Account
summary: Rory hid in the library from 15:40 until the alarm, listening. He never went into the drawing room.
details: 'Mr Rory was in the library from twenty to four, listening at the connecting door to hear the will. I was dusting the whole time. He never went in. When Mr Gerald fell he ran.'

title: Rory's Bus Ticket
summary: Rory arrived in Ashcombe village on the 15:35 bus, not at half past four.
details: Ridgeway & District bus ticket: Ridgeway to Ashcombe village, arriving 15:35, Saturday 14 July. Left on the bar of the Ashcombe Arms.
